idiom_name: module-scope Map held in module closure; the module is the single owner
implementation_notes: A module-scope Map keyed by string is the registry: it is created once per resolved module, stays unexported, and a top-level function returns the existing value or builds and stores a new one, so the class + private constructor + static map adds nothing over the closure. Node's single-threaded event loop means no lock is needed inside one isolate, but worker_threads, cluster forks and duplicated module instances each evaluate their own registry, so 'one per key' is really 'one per key per worker' - use a global symbol registry or a single entry point when instance identity must be process-wide.
pitfalls: Exporting the Map (or adding a register() helper) lets any importer overwrite entries, which is exactly what the pattern forbids.
Two copies of the package, or the same module loaded from two paths, yield two registries and two instances per key; identity-critical code needs one entry point.
Nothing cleans up: a Map keyed by request or user ids grows forever, so keys must come from a bounded domain or the module needs closeAll()/eviction.
